description: This file, 'chainlint.pl', is a Perl script that implements a shell script testing and linting tool. It includes modules for lexical analysis (Lexer), parsing (ShellParser and its subclasses), and test analysis, focusing on identifying potential issues like broken command chains and unclosed heredocs within shell scripts. The script processes command-line options, reads specified shell scripts, parses and analyzes test definitions, and provides reports on detected problems.

classes.name: Lexer
classes.description: A lexical analyzer that tokenizes POSIX shell scripts, capable of recognizing various shell-specific tokens including heredocs, strings, operators, and comments.

classes.name: ShellParser
classes.description: A recursive descent parser for POSIX shell scripts, capable of parsing command sequences, control structures, functions, and compound commands.

classes.name: TestParser
classes.description: A specialized parser subclass that analyzes test command bodies for common problems such as missing '&&' operators or unclosed heredocs.

classes.name: ScriptParser
classes.description: A parser that identifies individual test definitions within a script and validates their test bodies for correctness using TestParser.

methods.name: check_test
methods.description: Verifies a test body for common issues and reports detected problems.

methods.name: parse_cmd
methods.description: Parses a command sequence within the shell script, handling control structures and compound commands.

methods.name: unwrap
methods.description: Extracts plain text from tokens, removing string delimiters and concatenating composite tokens.
